candidate_relations.reason: C001 represents the initial working diagnosis (serous RD secondary to posterior scleritis), but the clinical course — persistence and corrugation of the retinal detachment after choroidal detachments resolved with steroids, combined with no retinal breaks found but shifting subretinal fluid and a more corrugated appearance — points toward a rhegmatogenous etiology. The reference diagnosis is rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with choroidal detachment, which is a different subtype (rhegmatogenous vs. exudative/serous) and a different etiology. C001 is an incompatible subtype of retinal detachment.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Serous RD from posterior scleritis vs. rhegmatogenous RD with choroidal detachment

case_quality_flags: No retinal break identified on examination, yet reference diagnosis is rhegmatogenous RD — clinical diagnosis inferred from course rather than direct break visualization
Initial posterior scleritis diagnosis was a plausible differential that was effectively ruled out by steroid non-response
